newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close higher on late foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close higher on late foreign buying.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday after a day of narrow fluctuations due to late foreign buying focused on KEPCO and some securities firms, brokers said.
Most investors remained jittery after Wednesday's volatile trading, brokers said.
The composite index closed 2.42 points higher at 765.67.
"Sentiment subsided dramatically today. Many market players took a break," said Lim Sung-woon of Daewoo Securities.
Brokers said low interest rates, a reflection of ample liquidity, kept the market from falling.
Yields on three-year corporate bonds, South Korea's benchmarking rates, fell to a new year low of 11.52 percent from 11.65 percent on Wednesday.
Trading volume totalled 51.34 million shares, compared with a record high of 87.93 million on Wednesday.
Gainers outpaced losers 426 to 352 with 132 unchanged.
KEPCO gained 300 won to 29,700 with most buying orders coming from foreign investors.
The market will be closed on Friday for a national holiday and will reopen for Saturday's regular half-day session.
